name: security-scim-provisioning-authority-review
intent: SCIM connector tenant, account and group-membership authority
artifacts: Connector credential/tenant mapping, SCIM schemas, PATCH handling, group membership and deprovisioning consumers.
trace: Trace external identifiers and connector authority into local account/group operations, especially replace/remove membership and disabled-user handling.
experiment: Use two owned tenants and synthetic users/groups; compare the rightful connector with cross-tenant identifier or PATCH membership substitution.
disproof: An externalId collision is not account compromise unless it selects or alters the wrong local principal.
repair: Bind connectors and operations to tenant/principal policy and verify create/update/deactivate plus unrelated tenant preservation.
branch_decisions: PATCH add/remove/replace and bulk semantics need the actual schema/path interpretation, especially group members and user active state. A connector may legitimately administer all users in its own tenant. Test cross-tenant mapping, immutable identity and deprovisioned-session effects as separate assertions.
operational_method: Retain the ordered PATCH operation list and filtered path interpretation, especially group members and active state. Distinguish connector externalId lookup from server-assigned id and inspect which tenant namespace each uses. Compare the before/after synthetic membership set, not only the final status code; a valid same-tenant administrative connector operation remains a positive control.
